findings.F1: Across all 6 coins, a coin's daily return scaled by its 20-day volatility predicts the next day's excess return with the opposite sign: the pooled slope is +0.16 % of next-day return per unit of fall, t 4.03 on 14,356 days. The effect holds in both halves of the windows (w1–w12 t 3.63, w13–w24 t 2.23), is positive on all 6 coins, and is strongest on XMR (t 4.46) and ETH (t 2.22).
findings.F2: That next-day reversal is mostly a rebound after falls. After a day down more than 1 volatility unit, the next day's excess return is +0.50 % (1,804 days), against −0.05 % after a day up more than 1 unit (1,983 days). After a fall of 1–2 units the t is 3.57 (1,444 days); after a fall of more than 2 units it is +0.61 % with t 2.00 (400 days). These one-day moves are 2.6 to 3.2 times the backtest's 0.19 % round trip.
findings.F3: A coin's past 5-day return predicts its excess return over the next 26 days on non-overlapping grids: slope +4.7 % per standard deviation, t 2.95 on 432 cases. The top quintile gives +9.2 % and the bottom −2.5 %. All 6 coins have a positive slope (lowest coin t 0.26), but the effect sits mostly in w13–w24 (t 3.02) against w1–w12 (t 1.08). It also shows over the next 10 days (t 2.95, 1,547 cases).
findings.F4: The past 26-day return also predicts the next 26 days (t 2.79, 432 cases), but its sign flips between halves (w1–w12 t −0.44, w13–w24 t 3.62). Over 10 days its early half is flat (t 0.03). It is not a stable pattern, unlike the shorter 5-day lookback in F3.
findings.F5: The tested regime does select better periods: in-regime grid cases have a 26-day excess return of +4.8 % (149 cases) against −1.7 % outside (427). Inside the regime, however, the thickness forecast leans the wrong way (t −1.62 on 107 cases). The past 26-day return (t 1.92) and the distance above the 26-day mean (t 1.84) grade the outcome better than thickness does.
findings.F6: Next-day excess returns by weekday are negative after Tuesday's and Thursday's bars (t −2.57 and −2.53, about 2,070 days each). Out of the roughly 15 angles examined, this does not stand out enough to count as a pattern.
findings.F7: The book earned a mean daily return of 0.033 % against 0.119 % for holding the coins (17,380 coin-days). It was flat on most days (interquartile range of daily returns 0 to 0), so it missed most of the coins' drift.

ideas.idea: The more a coin's daily return falls below zero, measured against its recent 20-day volatility, the more the coin rises over the next day above its normal drift.
ideas.consequence: A trader would lean long a coin for a day after an unusually sharp down day, and refuse to short into that fall.
ideas.name: Sharp daily fall rebounds next day

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's 5-day return, the larger its return over the next 26 days above its normal drift.
ideas.consequence: A trader would put more weight long on a coin with a strong last week, and less on one that fell over the past 5 days.
ideas.name: Last week's move continues monthly
